name: Green Belt
summary: In eastern Wetlands, Green Belt lies below the ridges of Grim Batol. Bog beasts, crocolisks, and toxic oozes roam its marshes, while Rethiel the Greenwarden keeps watch alone.

sections.title: A Wild and Contested Fen
sections.body: Green Belt fills the eastern interior of Wetlands, where mossy waters make travel hazardous. Massive crocolisks, shifting oozes, and shambling bog beasts roam the fen. Deep within it, a solitary watch post is manned by Rethiel the Greenwarden, a night elf who studies the fen's ecology and keeps its hostile creatures in check.

sections.title: Remnants of the Second War
sections.body: Wreckage from a Dragonmaw clan caravan lies scattered in the muck, left behind after the catastrophic battle at nearby Grim Batol. Crimson whelplings linger around the broken carts and crushed cages, reminders of the clan's past enslavement of Alexstrasza and her red dragon brood.

faq.q: Where is the Green Belt located?
faq.answer: Green Belt occupies the eastern half of Wetlands, along the soggy lowlands between the main road and the foothills rising toward Grim Batol.

Rethiel the Greenwarden is a night elf keeping watch alone in the Wetlands marsh. Far from his ancestral home of Kalimdor, he seeks to preserve nature's balance in the swamp and enlists travelers to deal with corrupting beasts and oozes.

faq.q: Why are there red whelps and broken wagons here?
aliases: why are there whelps in wetlands
faq.answer: The broken wagons are the remains of a Dragonmaw clan supply caravan caught in the aftermath of the Second War, when the orcs were routed from Grim Batol and their hold over the red dragonflight was shattered.

faq.q: What threats wander the Green Belt?
faq.answer: Dangerous crocolisks, toxic living oozes, and towering bog beasts roam Green Belt, blending into the sodden vegetation.

angles.text: As a night elf, you may find Rethiel the Greenwarden's lonely watch in an Eastern Kingdoms swamp surprising. His presence recalls the Cenarion circle and night elven devotion to healing wild lands wherever they lie.
As a druid, you can see how twisted oozes and unchecked bog beasts disrupt the marsh's natural harmony. The fen is a concern for keepers of the wild.
